title: Title verification before buying property - what lawyers actually check
p1:
A property can look perfect on paper and still become a legal nightmare.

Many buyers think title verification is just checking the seller's name on a document. That is only the beginning.
p2:
Lawyers don't just ask, "Who owns this property?" They investigate whether that ownership is legally clear.

They check past sale deeds, inheritance records, government records, existing loans, disputes, and whether previous transfers were valid. A missing link from years ago can create problems for a buyer today.
p3:
One thing many people don't know: even a registered document does not automatically guarantee a clean title. Registration records a transaction, but they do not always confirm that the seller had the full legal right to sell.

A proper title check helps identify risks before money changes hands.

Before buying property, don't just verify the building. Verify the story behind its ownership.
conclusion: Have you ever checked the ownership history of a property before buying, or did you assume registration was enough?
